interactions.summary: Jiang closes by arguing that empathy is necessary for cross-cultural work, for a less opaque China, and for a smoother and more peaceful Chinese rise.
interactions.speaker_attribution: Jiang answer continuing the prior question

interactions.summary: The host thanks Jiang and closes the interview.

claims.claim: Jiang says the future global workplace will require students who can not only work with other cultures but manage across cultures as well.
He argues Finland's emphasis on empathy better prepares students for that cross-cultural future, while China will struggle because it has not cultivated the same capacity.
Jiang says misunderstanding between China and the rest of the world persists because China cannot understand how the rest of the world thinks and is seen externally as a black box.
He argues educators should form a new generation of Chinese students with empathy and respect for other cultures so that China's rise can be smoother and more peaceful.

signature_moments.moment: China is described as a black box to the rest of the world because it cannot understand how outsiders think.
signature_moments.source_phrase: China right now is considered a black box
signature_moments.why_it_matters: It gives the empathy argument a geopolitical edge rather than leaving it as a soft educational virtue.

signature_moments.moment: Empathy becomes the educational condition for a smooth and peaceful Chinese rise.
signature_moments.source_phrase: make sure that China's rise is as smooth and as peaceful as possible
signature_moments.why_it_matters: It is Jiang's final compression of why schooling, social trust, and geopolitics belong in the same argument.

chronology_notes.note: The closing answer shifts from present educational diagnosis into a future-oriented argument about the kind of students a global economy and China's future rise will require.
